claim: For connected finite simple undirected graphs compared at the same order \\(n\\) and the same size \\(m\\), let \\(\\rho_A(G)\\) be the adjacency spectral radius and \\(\\rho_B(G)\\) the Hashimoto nonbacktracking spectral radius. No graph pair with \\(n\\le5\\) receives opposite strict rankings from \\(\\rho_A\\) and \\(\\rho_B\\). Order \\(n=6\\) is sharp: at common size \\(m=7\\), let \\(G\\) have edges \\({01,02,03,04,05,23,45}\\) and let \\(H\\) have edges \\({04,05,13,14,23,24,34}\\). Then \\(\\rho_A(G)\\approx2.709275359436925>2.705586727307842\\approx\\rho_A(H)\\), while \\(\\rho_B(G)=\\sqrt[3]{3}\\approx1.442249570307409<1.521379706804568\\approx\\rho_B(H)\\), where \\(\\rho_B(H)\\) is the positive root of \\(x^3-x-2=0\\). Thus the adjacency-based inverse spectral threshold surrogate \\(1/\\rho_A\\) ranks \\(G\\) as more vulnerable, whereas the nonbacktracking/message-passing inverse spectral threshold surrogate \\(1/\\rho_B\\) ranks \\(H\\) as more vulnerable. The lower-order exclusion is exhaustive over connected graph isomorphism classes and uses exact characteristic polynomials with Sturm root isolation.
integrity: All connected graph isomorphism classes through five vertices are exhaustively generated. Adjacency Perron roots and Ihara--Bass nonbacktracking roots are compared using exact rational polynomial arithmetic and Sturm isolation; the six-vertex witness is replayed from its explicit edge sets.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns connected finite simple undirected graphs compared at common order and size, and it compares adjacency and nonbacktracking spectral quantities or their inverse threshold surrogates. It does not assert that both inverses are exact epidemic thresholds for one universal stochastic model; their modeling interpretations have different approximation regimes.
title: Six vertices are the sharp fixed-order-and-size reversal boundary for adjacency and nonbacktracking spectral radii
